info.title: Asolytics Public API
info.description: > **Beta version.** The API is ready for production use, but it is still evolving: parameters, response formats and token costs may change. Watch the changelog and keep your integration tolerant to new response fields.

get.description:
App Store Connect analytics of the project's app by day, week or month — the data of the *App Store analytics* page of the dashboard, read through the project's App Store analytics connection (the connection of the project owner or of a team lead above them; a user the project is shared with reads through it too). When an incentive-traffic integration is connected, motivated installs are moved out of `Search` into a separate `Incentive` traffic source, as in the dashboard.

The request and the answer have the same frame as `/v1/analytics/google-play/time-series`: `group_by`, `group_values[]`, `filters[][]`, and `series: [{group: {key, title}, metrics: {: {total, type, points}}}]`.

**What one request can ask** (App Store Connect's own limits — anything else is refused with 422 before the store is asked, nothing charged):
- `measures[]` — one or two of `proceeds`, `sales`, `totalDownloads` (= `units` + `redownloads`), `redownloads`, `units` (first-time downloads), `pageViewCount`, `impressionsTotal`, `impressionsTotalUnique`. Apple refuses three or more with a breakdown; every series carries all the requested measures.
- `group_by` (required) — `country`, `traffic_source`, `app_referrer` or `web_referrer`.
- **Apple returns only the top 10 groups**, ranked by the first measure. Particular groups can be asked for only by country: `group_by=country` with `group_values[]` (ISO codes, up to 10 — ten named countries always come back in full); for more countries, split them into calls of 10. `group_values[]` with another `group_by` is a 422.
- `filters[country][]` (up to 10 ISO codes, summed) and `filters[traffic_source][]` narrow the data; values of one filter are OR-ed, the two filters AND-ed. The `group_by` dimension cannot also be a filter (with `group_by=country` pick the countries with `group_values[]`).
- `filters[traffic_source][]` does not combine with `group_by=app_referrer` / `web_referrer`: referrers exist only for referral traffic.

**Traffic sources** (`group.key` with `group_by=traffic_source`, values of `filters[traffic_source][]`): `Search` (App Store search), `Other` (App Store browse), `AppRef` (app referrer), `WebRef` (web referrer), `EventNotification`, `Volume Purchase`, `Unknown`. The answer may carry more sources than Apple's — `Incentive`, and others added by integrations connected to the account (they cannot be filtered by); a moved amount is taken from the source it belongs to, so the sources still add up to Apple's total and none goes below zero. Country groups are keyed by ISO code. There is no `overall` series: App Store answers always come broken down.

**History** reaches back as far as the plan allows (`store_analytics_max_deep`, 403 otherwise). The last one or two days may still be incomplete in App Store Connect.

**Retries.** The store is read through shared connections and answers are cached for an hour. `429` with `reason: busy` — the connections serve other requests, retry after the `Retry-After` seconds; `503` `warming_up` — the store session is being signed in, retry in about a minute; `503` `unavailable` — the store or the session failed, retry later. Calls are also limited per minute per account (the team owner for members) — `429` with `Retry-After`; a call refused as invalid (422) before the store is asked does not count against the limit. `409` — the App Store analytics cannot be read for the project: `reason: not_connected` — it is not connected (`how_to_connect` says how), `reason: insufficient_permissions` — the access granted in App Store Connect lacks the permissions to read the analytics (`how_to_fix` says what to change; retrying does not help until it is fixed).

**Costs:** 10 tokens per call that returns data — an empty answer and a cached one included. Validation errors, 403, 404, 409, 429 and 503 are free. At least 10 tokens on balance are required before the store is asked (402).

get.summary: Google Play analytics: time series and table
get.description:
Play Console acquisition of the project's app — store listing visitors, installers and conversion rate, the data of the *Google Play analytics* page of the dashboard, read through the project's Play Console connection (the connection of the project owner or of a team lead above them; a user the project is shared with reads through it too). The request and the `series` have the same frame as `/v1/analytics/app-store/time-series`. One call returns both parts of the page:
- `series` — the **daily** series of the overall (`group.key` = `overall`) and of the requested `group_values[]` only, all three metrics each;
- `table` — totals of the range over **every** value of the `group_by` dimension Google reports (not only `group_values[]`), each with the value of the previous period of the same length and the change. Start with no `group_values[]` to see in `table` which values carry data, then ask for their series.

**What one request can ask:**
- `group_by` — the breakdown dimension (default `country`): `country`, `traffic_source`, `search_term`, `store_listing`, `language`, `install_state`, `utm_source`, `utm_campaign`, `custom_audience`.
- `group_values[]` — up to 50 values of the `group_by` dimension to draw a series for (countries as ISO codes).
- `filters[][]` (same dimension names, up to 50 values each) narrow both parts — values of one dimension are OR-ed, dimensions AND-ed. The `group_by` dimension cannot also be a filter (422) — pick its values with `group_values[]`.
- Values come from `/v1/analytics/google-play/dimension-values` (or the `table` keys); a value Google does not list for the app is refused with 422 before the data is asked for (free). Search terms are Google's top list only.

**History:** Play Console keeps about the **last 90 days**: a `date_from` earlier than 90 days before today (UTC) is refused with 422 (free), the message names the earliest allowed date. Also capped by the plan's store analytics history (`store_analytics_max_deep`, 403 with `earliest_date`).

**Retries.** The store is read through shared connections and answers are cached for an hour. `429` with `reason: busy` — retry after the `Retry-After` seconds; `503` `unavailable` — the store or the session failed, retry later. Calls are also limited per minute per account (the team owner for members) — `429` with `Retry-After`; a call refused as invalid (422) before the store is asked does not count against the limit. `409` — Google Play Console is not connected for the project (the body says how to connect it).

**Costs:** 10 tokens per call that returns data (series and table together) — an empty answer and a cached one included. Validation errors, 403, 404, 409, 429 and 503 are free. At least 10 tokens on balance are required before the store is asked (402).

get.description:
The values Play Console lists for the project's app in every analytics dimension, keyed by the dimension names of `group_by` / `filters[…]` — the keys to pass in `group_values[]` and `filters[][]` of `/v1/analytics/google-play/time-series`. Each value comes with its title and the installers count Google ranks the list by; search terms are Google's top list only. The list is cached for a day.

`409` — Google Play Console is not connected for the project (the body says how to connect it); `429` / `503`, retries and the per-minute limit — as in the time series.

**Costs:** 1 token per call (a cached answer included). 404, 409, 429 and 503 are free.

get.description:
Returns monthly **estimated** installs for a single application across every country we currently track (or only the `country_codes[]` you pass), for each month in the requested range. Values are estimates derived from store signals — not measured installs — and are emitted as `null` for months we couldn't estimate (sparsely-tracked apps, or the most recent month while it's still being computed). Returns 404 if the `origin_id` doesn't resolve to a known application.

**Costs:** 10 tokens per emitted (country, month) pair carrying a non-null value (`0` counts; `null` does not). Minimum 10 tokens per call — charged even if the entire grid is null.

get.description:
Returns the ranking history of a single application in the given country, as a paginated flat list of `{date, keyword, position}` rows — one row per scanned (date, keyword) pair the app ranks for, across every keyword we cover (no keyword filter). Supports a position-range filter and sorting by `date`, `position` or `keyword`; pipeline is filter → sort → paginate, so `total` / `total_pages` reflect the filtered universe. The window cannot exceed **7 days** and `date_from` cannot reach further back than the 1st of (current month − 5 months). Returns 404 if the `origin_id` doesn't resolve to a known application; apps with no scans in range return an empty page (still billed the minimum).

**Costs:** `max(5, ceil(rows_on_page / 20))` tokens — 1 token per started bucket of 20 rows on the returned page, with a floor of 5 charged even on empty responses.

get.description:
Returns what changed in an app's store listing, day by day (the Update Timeline): title, subtitle, description, screenshots, icon, version, size and preview videos. Each day lists one **fact** per changed type; a fact's `changes` group the locales that changed from the same state to the same state, each with `before` (the previous state and the day it was first seen) and `after`. Only days with changes are listed, newest first. History goes back about 6 months (`date_from` no earlier than the 1st of the current month − 6 months), at most 90 days per call. Use `types[]` and `locales[]` to fetch only what you need — they also make the call cheaper. `size` exists on the App Store only and comes with a release: a release that kept the size is not a size change. Screenshots and videos are compared per device, so only the changed devices are shown. `before` is null when a locale or a device appears for the first time. Returns 404 if the `origin_id` doesn't resolve to a known application.

**Costs:** 1 token per returned fact — a (date, type) pair with a change: a title updated in many locales on one day is 1 fact, a title and screenshots changed on the same day are 2. A request with no changes is free.

get.description:
Returns the app card: icon, rating and number of ratings, developer (name, site), app site, privacy policy URL, store categories, release and last update dates, last version, size (App Store only), average days between releases, age in days, in-app purchase price range in USD and when its metadata last changed. Pass `country_code` to also get the rating, number of ratings and whether the app is live in that country (`country` block); for the list of all countries where the app is live use `/v1/applications/availability`. Without it `rating` is the mean of the latest per-country ratings and `votes_count` their sum. Ratings come from scans of the last month only: an app not scanned for a month has `rating: null`. For the rating over time use `/v1/applications/ratings`; for installs and revenue, `/v1/applications/installs` and `/v1/applications/revenue`; for the title/subtitle/description text, `/v1/applications/metadata`. The app's price and age rating are not provided. Returns 404 if the `origin_id` doesn't resolve to a known application; 422 for a `country_code` the app's store does not have.

**Costs:** 15 tokens per call without `country_code`, 20 tokens with it.

Returns the app's average rating and total number of ratings day by day in each requested country, as the store showed them on the days we scanned the app. Both are the store's running values (the number of ratings is a total, not the day's new ratings). History goes back about 6 months (`date_from` no earlier than the 1st of the current month − 6 months), at most 90 days per call. Days we did not scan are absent — the history can have gaps; a country with no scans in the window (or one the app's store does not have) comes back with an empty `history`. Returns 404 if the `origin_id` doesn't resolve to a known application. For the latest rating alone use `/v1/applications/info`.

**Costs:** 3 tokens per returned (day, country) pair. A request that returns no days is free.

Each transaction carries its `cause` (the endpoint key that triggered the debit, `null` for system rows like the monthly balance renewal), a signed `amount` (debits are negative), the timestamp, and a pointer back to the originating public-API request (`null` for system rows). The full `cause_details` payload is intentionally not exposed here — treat the list as a quick activity feed, not a complete audit trail.

**Costs:** 1 token per call.

Competitor state is tracked in the project store's US country (the public API hides per-country state — each app has exactly one state in the list). post.description:
Marks apps (by their store `origin_id`) as `competitor`, `non_competitor` or `indirect_competitor` for the project. Pass **either** `competitor_origin_id` (one app) **or** `competitor_origin_ids` (up to 100 apps in one call), not both. Idempotent — re-marking with the same state is a no-op; re-marking with a different state moves the app to that state.

The response lists what happened to every requested app: `processed` — marked; `not_found` — no app is known for that `origin_id` (take ids from `/v1/competitors/finder` or `/v1/live-search`); `skipped` — the app belongs to the other store than the project's (a competitor must be in the project's store). With the single `competitor_origin_id` an unknown app is a 404 instead, as before.

**Plan limits:** marking spends the project's per-plan allowance — direct and indirect competitors share `max_competitors_project`, non-competitors have `max_not_competitors_project`. Only apps not yet counted there spend it (re-marking, or moving an app between direct and indirect, is free). If the call would go over the allowance it answers 403 with the limit key, and **nothing** is marked or charged. Check the room left beforehand with `/v1/subscription/limits?project_id=…`.

**Costs:** 1 token per app in the request — **every** requested app is billed, including those reported as `not_found` or `skipped` (an `origin_id` repeated in the list counts once); a single `competitor_origin_id` costs 1. Charged before marking; a single-app call answered with 404 is free.

get.description:
Suggests apps that compete with the project app in a store country — the same search as the *Competitors Finder* of the dashboard. Candidates are drawn from the store tops of the project's tracked keywords and of its recommended keywords, from related and similar apps, and come ordered by relevance (apps with at least 300 ratings in the country first). Each candidate is `{origin_id, title, subtitle}`; why an app was suggested is not returned. Apps already marked in the project (`competitor`, `non_competitor` or `indirect_competitor`, see `/v1/competitors`) and the project app itself are never suggested — after marking candidates with `/v1/competitors/mark` (it takes up to 100 `competitor_origin_ids`) the next call shows the rest. For more about a candidate use `/v1/applications/metadata`.

**Slow first call:** the search reads the project's recommended keywords for the country; if they were never computed for this project and country, this call computes them first, which can take **several minutes** (later calls are fast). Expect a long response on the first call for a new country, and retry rather than call in parallel.

**Costs:** 20 tokens per call, charged after the result is built; requires at least 20 tokens on balance before the search starts (otherwise 402, nothing computed).

post.description:
Orders an on-demand re-scan of the store top for the given phrases in a (store, country). The call returns as soon as the re-check is queued — the fresh positions land in our storage a few minutes later and can be read through `/v1/keywords/ranking` or `/v1/applications/ranking`. Supply `webhook.url` to be notified: we POST one message per phrase as soon as its scan is done. Up to 500 phrases per request; duplicates (case-insensitive) are collapsed and billed once.

**Webhook payload:** `{request: {id}, task: {keyword, country_code, store}, result: {status}}` where `request.id` is the `request.id` of this response. With `webhook.include_positions = true` the result also carries `positions` — the scanned top as `[{position, item: {origin_id}}, …]`, capped at 50 entries; an empty array means the scan found nothing. We ignore the response body and only look at the status code: a non-200 is retried twice with a growing delay, then dropped. Redirects are not followed and the request times out after a few seconds. The callback host must resolve to a public address — private, loopback and link-local targets are rejected and the notice is dropped without retries.

**Costs:** 15 tokens per unique phrase, **+1** with a webhook, **+1** more with `include_positions` — so 15 / 16 / 17 per phrase, charged when the re-check is queued (not when it completes).

get.description:
Returns a snapshot of one or more latest metrics for up to 250 keywords in a (store, country). Each keyword in the response appears exactly once in the same order and casing as the request; duplicate keywords are deduplicated. Only the requested metrics are present on each keyword object. Metrics that resolve to null (no scan data available) are omitted from the billed pairs but still appear in the response as null.

**Metric availability by store:**
- `popularity` — App Store only (raw scan); Google Play omits the `popularity` field, only `mlp_popularity` is returned.
- `max_popularity` — App Store: `year_max_popularity` (raw) and `synthetic_year_max_popularity` (mlp). Google Play: `mlp_max_popularity` only (`all_time_max_popularity`).
- `impressions` — App Store: estimated daily impressions derived from both real and synthetic popularity. Google Play: `mlp_impressions` only.
- `difficulty` — both stores, single value (no real/mlp split).
- `language` — both stores, country-independent, single value.

**Costs:** per (keyword, metric) pair where the resolved value is non-null — 5 tokens for `popularity` and `max_popularity`, 1 token for `impressions`, `difficulty` and `language`; minimum 1 token per call.

post.description:
Adds an app to the caller's projects, exactly like adding an app in the dashboard. The app is addressed by its store `origin_id` (App Store numeric id or Google Play package name); the store is taken from the app. The app must already be known to Asolytics: if it is not (404), find it first with `/v1/live-search` — every app a live search returns is saved, and then this call succeeds. `country_code` is the country the project starts in (it gets the first warm-up); it must be in `/v1/common-catalogs/countries` of the app's store, otherwise 422 before anything is billed.

What happens on success: the project uses one slot of the plan's `max_apps` limit (counted for the whole team, see `/v1/subscription/limits`), then — asynchronously, in the background — tracking/ranking/metadata/recommended keywords are warmed up for every country of the store, the ASO Score is calculated, and the owner is subscribed to the weekly e-mail report for `country_code`. Data appears over the next minutes; the new project is immediately visible in `/v1/projects/list`.

One project per app per user: if the caller already has this app (also when it is archived) the answer is 409 with the existing `project_id` and `is_archived` — nothing is billed. An archived project cannot be restored through the API, only in the dashboard. At most 15 successful creations per hour per account (a team shares the owner's allowance); over it — 429 with `Retry-After`.

**Costs:** 10 tokens per created project, billed before the project is created. Rejected calls (validation, 403, 404, 409, 429, 503) are free.

put.description:
Turns on (or changes) auto-approve of recommended keywords for the project — the same as saving *Auto-approve* in the dashboard. **Full replacement:** the body becomes the project's only settings; countries and filters not in the body are dropped. To add a country or change one filter, first read the current settings with `GET /v1/recommended-keywords/autoapprove-settings`, edit them and send the whole set here.

Body: `country_codes` — the countries auto-approve runs in (from `/v1/common-catalogs/countries` of the project's store, otherwise 422); `filters` — the criteria for those countries, all set ones must match: ranges `{from, to}` (inclusive) `range_sap` (current popularity), `range_max_sap` (year-max popularity), `range_impression` (estimated daily impressions), `range_difficulty`, `range_rank` (the project app's position; unranked keywords never match), `range_top_competitors` (marked competitors in the top 10, `includeIndirect` to count indirect ones too), `range_top_non_competitors`; lists `{list: […]}` `sources` (`import`, `meta`, `related`, `competitors`, `rankings`, `suggestions`) and `language` (e.g. `English`). The example sets every criterion to show the shape — a typical rule uses two or three; `specific` — optional per-country overrides, each country must be in `country_codes`, and such a country uses only its own filters. Every country must end up with at least one criterion.

**Effect:** every save recalculates the project's recommended keywords in every listed country and adds the matching ones — not tracked yet and not declined — to tracking, in the background (minutes for a large country). After that it keeps running on every regular recalculation until stopped with `DELETE`. Added keywords use the plan's `max_keywords` limit (when it is full nothing more is added); auto-approve stops adding in a country once it has 10 000 tracked keywords. Requires EDIT access. At most 10 successful saves per hour per project; over it — 429 with `Retry-After`.

**Costs:** 10 tokens per save, billed before saving. Rejected calls (validation, 403, 404, 429) are free; keywords added to tracking by auto-approve are not billed.
